reason: A second, different value for a PROV attribute raises `ProvException` with `Cannot have more than one value for attribute <attr>` and stores nothing. The nine input rows are `constant` (a collection pair and two entities), `constant-one-shot-iterator` (the same pairs from an iterator), `string` (the collection key written as the string `prov:collection`), `none-collection` (a `None` collection), `no-collection` (two entities only), `unresolvable-none-pair` (a `zz:x` pair with a `None` value, a collection and two entities), `second-call` (a later call adds the second entity to a record that holds the collection and the first entity), `two-collections` (two different `prov:collection` values, where the assertion is on `prov:collection`) and `derivation` (a collection and two used entities on a derivation, where the assertion is on `prov:usedEntity`). Under #700 and spec 5 section 4.2, the single-value rule holds for every PROV attribute of every record type with no `prov:collection` lift.

A read through an accessor, a property, `unified()`, `flattened()`, the graph and dot converters or a writer leaves the keys of every record's `_attributes` as they were. Under #696 and spec 5 section 4.1, a read creates no attribute entry.

A second, different `prov:time` on a generation raises `ProvException` and leaves the `_attributes` keys and `attributes` as they were. Under spec 5 section 4.1 (#696) and 4.2 (#700), a rejected value is not stored and a call that stores nothing changes nothing.

On a fresh entity `get_asserted_types()` equals `set()` and is falsy, `.value` equals `set()` and `.label` is `"ex:e"`. The #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md` (2.x return types), and the `label` fallback to the identifier text. No source found for the label fallback.

On an entity built with `1` on `ex:v`, `prov:type` or `prov:value`, adding `2` to the set that `get_attribute("ex:v")`, `get_asserted_types()` or `.value` returns leaves the next call to the same accessor equal to `{1}`. HISTORY.md's 3.0.0 entry says that `ProvRecord.get_attribute`, `ProvRecord.get_asserted_types` and `ProvRecord.value` build their set fresh on every call, so mutating it never reaches the record, and the #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md` warns that mutating a `get_asserted_types()` result no longer writes through. A set cached on the record, planted in any one of the three accessors, fails only this test's row for that accessor, and before the test the same fault in `ProvRecord.get_asserted_types` or `ProvRecord.value` failed no test in the suite. The maintainer added the test after the audit of this module found that gap, and folded `test_attribute_merging.py::test_get_attribute_returns_a_copy_not_the_live_container` into it as the `get-attribute` row. That test added `999` to the set `get_attribute("ex:v")` returned and checked the next call gave `{2}`, and the row makes the same mutation and second read with `1` and `2`, so nothing was lost.

Removed. After `set_time(startTime=...)` the attribute entry of the record had the type name `TypedValueSet` and `get_startTime()` returned the time. The classifier gave rewrite, because the test pinned the private class name `TypedValueSet`. The maintainer sent it through the layers as a removal, and #34 does not describe its input, since #34 is about extra attribute values such as `2` and `2.0`. test_extras.py::test_use_set_time_helpers takes over the storage type, because it compares a `set_time` activity with one built with `startTime=` and `endTime=`. The comparison with `==` enters `ProvDocument.__eq__`, then `ProvBundle.__eq__` through `super().__eq__`, which hashes each record through `ProvRecord.__hash__`, which calls `ProvRecord._typed_attributes`, which calls `value_keys()` on each stored container. test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_start_only takes over the start-only `get_startTime()` line. The verifier and the judge planted faults in `ProvActivity.set_time` (a plain set, a plain list, and a plain set for the start time only, in place of `TypedValueSet`). Each failed test_extras.py::test_use_set_time_helpers with an `AttributeError` raised in `ProvRecord._typed_attributes`, because a plain set or list has no `value_keys`. For the plain set and the plain list it was the only failing test once this removed test was deselected. Storing the start only when an end is given failed test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_start_only, and swapping the keys failed it, test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_both and test_model.py::test_activity_set_time_end_only. The mutation run over records.py left no mutant undetected.

Removed. After two `ProvRecord.add_asserted_type` calls, `get_asserted_types()` has length 2. test_attribute_merging.py::test_get_asserted_types_returns_a_plain_set_and_is_type_preserving takes over, because it makes the same two calls on a fresh entity and asserts the full set, which implies the length. The verifier's three faults in `ProvRecord.add_asserted_type` (store the first only, overwrite, store to a copy) each failed the takeover, the removed test owned no arc, and the mutation run left no mutant undetected.

Removed. An entity built with `1` and `True` on one attribute kept both, read back through `attributes` with their types (#34). It is now the `bool-and-int` row of test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_differently_typed_values, with the same input and the same assertion. The merge check showed identical arcs for the row in `TypedValueSet.add` and `_value_key`, and the mutation run over records.py and _values.py changed no mutant's status.

An entity built with two values on one attribute keeps both, read back through `attributes` with their types, for the pairs `(2, 2.0)`, `(1, True)` and `(2, True)` (rows `int-and-float`, `bool-and-int` and `int-and-unequal-bool`). Under #34, attribute sets used to drop a Python-equal but differently typed value, and the module docstring names construction as one of the places it happened. The row `int-and-unequal-bool` is the control pair, because `2 != True` and so it never collapsed. Merged from test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_python_equal_differently_typed_values, test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_bool_vs_int and test_attribute_merging.py::test_int_vs_bool_that_are_not_equal_is_not_a_regression_case, which differed only in value pair and expected set. Every input and the one assertion stay, with no branch on a parameter. The merge check showed identical arcs per row in `TypedValueSet.add` and `_value_key`, and the mutation run over records.py and _values.py changed no mutant's status. The judge renamed the merged function from test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_python_equal_differently_typed_values, because the `int-and-unequal-bool` row is not a Python-equal pair.

Removed. An entity built with `2` and `2.0` on one attribute kept both, read back through `attributes` with their types (#34). It is now the `int-and-float` row of test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_differently_typed_values, with the same input and the same assertion. The merge check showed identical arcs for the row in `TypedValueSet.add` and `_value_key`, and the mutation run over records.py and _values.py changed no mutant's status.
Two entities with the same typed values on `ex:v` and `ex:w`, asserted in opposite order, are equal and hash alike. Under #34, the typed-value comparison must still ignore the order of assertion.
An entity built with `("ex:v", 2)` twice holds the single value `2`. Under #34, only Python-equal values of different types stay apart, a true duplicate still collapses.

`get_asserted_types()` after two `add_asserted_type` calls returns an instance of set equal to the two names. The maintainer decision in the module docstring and the #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md` say that `ProvRecord.get_asserted_types` keeps its 2.x return type. It took over `test_attribute_merging.py::test_add_asserted_type_mutates_live_storage_not_a_copy`, which made the same two `ProvRecord.add_asserted_type` calls on a fresh entity and asserted only a length of 2, which this test's `== {foo, bar}` implies. The verifier planted three faults in `ProvRecord.add_asserted_type` (store only the first type, overwrite, store to a copy), and each failed this test with the removed test deselected. Later audit: the test's comment says `prov:type` values are always QualifiedNames that never collapse, and its name says type-preserving, but the docstring of `ProvRecord.get_asserted_types` and #748 say a string or a number can be asserted as a type and that `5` and `5.0` collapse; rewrite both.

Removed. Adding `999` to the set that `get_attribute("ex:v")` returned left the next call equal to `{2}`. `test_attribute_merging.py::test_accessors_return_a_fresh_set_on_every_call` takes over as its `get-attribute` row, which makes the same mutation and second read on `ex:v` with `1` and `2`. A set cached on the record planted in `ProvRecord.get_attribute` fails that row and no other test. The maintainer ruled the fold-in on review.

`get_attribute("ex:v")` on a record holding `2` and `2.0` returns an instance of set equal to `{2}`. The maintainer decision in the module docstring and the #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md` say that `get_attribute()` keeps its 2.x return type.

Two entities with one identifier, one holding `2` and `2.0` on `ex:v` and the other holding `2`, have `attributes` of length 2 and 1, are unequal and hash differently. Under #34, record equality and hashing must see the retained typed values. It took over `test_attribute_merging.py::test_records_with_different_retained_value_sets_are_not_equal`, which built the same two entities from the same identifier and asserted the same inequality and hash inequality, without the `attributes` lengths. The verifier planted four faults in `ProvRecord.__eq__` and `ProvRecord.__hash__` (comparing `frozenset(self.attributes)`, comparing attribute names only, and dropping the attribute term from the hash), and each failed this test as well as the removed one. `ProvRecord._typed_attributes` is the typed comparison they bypass.

Removed. An entity built with `2` and `True` on one attribute kept both, read back through `attributes` with their types; `2 != True`, so the pair never collapsed (#34). It is now the `int-and-unequal-bool` row of test_attribute_merging.py::test_construction_retains_differently_typed_values, with the same input, the same assertion and its comment. The merge check showed identical arcs for the row in `TypedValueSet.add` and `_value_key`, and the mutation run over records.py and _values.py changed no mutant's status.

On the record's own per-attribute container holding `2` and `2.0`, membership finds each, `3` is absent, `discard(2.0)` leaves only `2` and `discard(3)` changes nothing (#34). No public call reaches `TypedValueSet.discard`. The judge ran the whole suite with both methods wrapped to record their callers, and only this test calls `discard`. Its `discard(2.0)` line asserts that `2` stays, which guards against a `TypedValueSet.discard` keyed on Python equality, but no fault was planted for `discard`. A `TypedValueSet.__contains__` keyed on Python equality (`any(value == v for v in self._index.values())`) failed no test in the whole suite, this one included, because `2`, `2.0` and `3` give the same membership answers either way. The maintainer accepted the query and kept the membership lines because `Set` equality relies on `__contains__`. By that fault run, those lines pin no type-aware behaviour on their own. A separate change bases `TypedValueSet` on collections.abc.Set, deletes `discard` and cuts this test to its membership lines.

Two `xsd:decimal` literals `"10"` and `"10.00"` on one attribute leave one value, and it is the first one asserted. Under #77, decimal literals compare by value, and the first value asserted is the one kept.

`Literal("hi", langtag="en")` and `Literal("hi", langtag="EN")` on one attribute leave one value, and its tag is `en`. Under #259, language tags compare case-insensitively, and the first value asserted is the one kept.

A document with `2` and `2.0` on one attribute equals its reload from JSON, XML and RDF, and the reloaded record holds both typed values. Under #34, the retained values must survive serialisation round trips.

A record that was read before extra attributes were added serialises to PROV-JSON, PROV-JSONLD and PROV-N identically to one never read, with attributes in assertion order. Under #696 and spec 5 section 4.1, output key order follows the order values were asserted.

Removed. Two entities with one identifier, one holding `2` and `2.0` on `ex:v` and the other holding `2`, are unequal and hash differently (#34). test_attribute_merging.py::test_hash_distinguishes_typed_values_even_when_attributes_property_collapses takes over, because it builds the same two entities and asserts the same inequality and hash inequality, plus the `attributes` lengths. The verifier's four faults in `ProvRecord.__eq__` and `ProvRecord.__hash__` failed the takeover as well, the removed test owned no arc, and the mutation run left no mutant undetected.

After `add_attributes([("ex:v", 2.0)])` on an entity that holds `2`, `attributes` shows both `(int, 2)` and `(float, 2.0)`. Under #34, the module docstring names separate `add_attributes()` calls as one of the three input shapes.

`unified()` on two same-identifier entities with different `prov:startTime` extra attributes raises `ProvException` and not `ProvUnificationError`. Under #253 and the maintainer ruling in the test, the single-value guard predates the unification work and stays a plain `ProvException`.

Two same-identifier entities asserting `2` and `2.0` on `ex:v` unify to one record that holds both values. Under #34, the module docstring names `unified()`'s extra-attribute union as one of the three input shapes.

A value set loaded from 3.2.x state holding a raw `Identifier` value writes in PROV-N as an `xsd:anyURI` literal that reads back as `Literal("http://example.org/x", XSD_ANYURI)`. Under #658, a raw `Identifier` value from an old pickle must still write as `xsd:anyURI`.

A value set rebuilt through `__setstate__` from the 3.2.x state `{(int, 5): 5}` contains `5`, iterates as `[5]` and equals the live container. `HISTORY.md` says `Identifier`, `QualifiedName`, `Namespace` and `Literal` load pickles written by earlier releases, and the 3.3.0 how-to says a `Literal` is checked on load from a pickle of an earlier release. No source found for the value set itself.

`.value` on a record holding `prov:value` `2` and `2.0` returns an instance of set equal to `{2}`. The maintainer decision in the module docstring and the #34 row of `docs/upgrading-3.0.md` say that `.value` keeps its 2.x return type.
